newsitem.title: USA: U.S. indicts three men for smuggling Asians.
newsitem.headline: U.S. indicts three men for smuggling Asians.

text.p: A U.S. grand jury on Tuesday indicted three New York men with attempting to smuggle more then 100 Asians into the United States by ship, the U.S. Attorney for Massachusetts said.

The three men, Hui Lin, 34, Yiu Ming Kwan, 45 and Nai Fook Li, 30, all of New York City, allegedly smuggled more than 100 Asians on a cargo ship to a prearranged point in the Atlantic Ocean, where they were loaded onto a smaller vessel to be transported to the Massachusetts shore, the Attorney's office said.
The three agreed to pay a minimum of $500,000 to the owner of the smaller ship, who was actually an undercover agent for the Immigration and Naturalisation Service.
The trio were charged with two counts of conspiracy to commit alien smuggling and two counts of attempted alien smuggling.

If convicted of attempted smuggling, the three men face up to 10 years in prison per alien, as well as a $250,000 fine. The maximum penalty for conspiracy to smuggle is five years imprisonment and a $250,000 fine.
